cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Request an Exception
cards.instruction: Get someone to bend one rule first so you can treat the decision as a precedent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Could my bicycle come inside the cafe just this once? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only because it's raining.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Wonderful. I'll note rain as an accepted condition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tomorrow it's Jo on the counter. She'll put it back outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then leave Jo a note: 'Bicycle admitted in rain.' I'll show her that before I show her the bicycle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could my bicycle come inside the cafe just this once?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only because it's raining.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. I'll note rain as an accepted condition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tomorrow it's Jo on the counter. She'll put it back outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then leave Jo a note: 'Bicycle admitted in rain.' I'll show her that before I show her the bicycle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me submit the form tomorrow. Today can be a trial extension.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody's had an extension before.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we can discover whether it harms the form.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One day. No more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. Next time we won't be discussing an untested idea.

cards.title: Record My Contribution
cards.instruction: Get your contribution formally recognized, recorded, or repeated where it cannot be quietly forgotten.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Please put 'roof repaired by Pat' in the village minutes. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We all know you fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. The minutes weren't there with a ladder. They need telling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We'll thank you at the party.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the roof line, write 'thanks pending' so we remember.

beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.text: Will you put my name under 'cake design' before you frame our club's prize certificate?

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Choose the Precedent
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which rule, custom, or prior decision will govern what happens now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. The handbook says lock the hall at six. Our festival permit says stay open till eight. Which governs tonight? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Keep the front open and lock the back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. So the permit governs public access, and the handbook governs everything else?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Including the kitchen closing at six.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then are we canceling the seven-o'clock supper, or does the permit govern kitchens too?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The handbook says lock the hall at six. Our festival permit says stay open till eight. Which governs tonight?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Keep the front open and lock the back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So the permit governs public access, and the handbook governs everything else?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Including the kitchen closing at six.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then are we canceling the seven-o'clock supper, or does the permit govern kitchens too?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Who gets the head seat: Grandma or the birthday child? We have traditions for both.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Put two chairs there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. Which tradition decides who gets served first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Serve them together. Except there's only one birthday pudding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose before I bring it in: elders first or birthdays first? I can divide the pudding once somebody's had the wish.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Interpret the Custom
cards.instruction: Ask them to apply an ambiguous custom where the wording is unclear. Treat their interpretation as the real test of loyalty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Before I leave for my shift, how much lasagne will you save me? Family custom says 'a proper portion.' Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It doesn't say how big.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Then I'll find out what 'proper' means when it's for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your brothers want seconds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Save mine before you serve those. I'd like being expected home to count before being hungry twice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I leave for my shift, how much lasagne will you save me? Family custom says 'a proper portion.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It doesn't say how big.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll find out what 'proper' means when it's for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your brothers want seconds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Save mine before you serve those. I'd like being expected home to count before being hungry twice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our gardening club supports members 'where possible.' Will you sign my appeal against losing my allotment?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That could just mean wishing you luck.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You get to interpret it. I'd like to know whether membership reaches as far as your signature.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Some members want my name kept off it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the same words have to cover me and their disapproval. Whose comfort does 'possible' protect?

cards.title: Withdraw the Objection
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to drop a complaint, challenge, or special request and accept the official process.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Drop the demand to question our delivery driver. The missing-parcel claim goes through this form. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your form requires a photo of the parcel I haven't received.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Use a photo of your empty doorstep. That's the delivery location.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you stand in it holding today's newspaper?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, beside the doormat. Put me under 'supporting evidence,' and leave the driver off your witness list.

beats.text: Please drop the request for a private tea queue. Everyone at the fete uses this one.

beats.text: I donated the tent. Can't that count for something?
